main_body: Roofed well: a domed slate roof on two wooden posts, with a stone basin holding water below. The basin is the largest lower volume.
top_band: Basin column x=16: light-grey rim at row 30 (L185), then blue water at rows 31-34 (L108) as the visible inside, then a light front-lip at row 35 (L157). The roof column shows a light ridge at rows 1-2 over slate slope rows 3-14.
evidence: The basin reads as a 3/4 piece. Its top is a rim plus a water surface about 5 rows tall, with a light front-lip line at row 35 (L157). A darker row 36 (L80) sits under that line, then the grey front face runs rows 37-42. The roof is a tall slope with a light ridge and tile stripes, so its upper surface is visible rather than a flat line. The posts are open vertical supports with a dark underside at rows 15-17. No receding side faces. Weak points are the flat, painted-on look of the front and the lack of an inset front, but the top surfaces are there.

style.evidence: The candidate has 23 distinct colours and a median of 9 per tile. The references have 38-40 colours and a median of 17-20 per tile, so it is clearly thinner. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral (#231d28 and similar), a uniform near-black outline, against 1% and 33% in the references. The roof has some stripe and highlight work, but the stone basin front and posts are nearly flat tones with about 3 steps each. It looks flatter and more sticker-like than prop-well-roofed.
